Hi Lena — great to hear. Appreciate the clarity on what Finance/Procurement are looking for. Below are three workable structures we typically use, with pros/cons related to Net-90 exposure and discounting.

1) Full prepay (single upfront payment at execution)
  - Discount: 20% off hosted list for a 3-year, fully-prepaid commitment
  - Risk: Redwood assumes payment timing risk (no Net-90); suitable if customer can prepay from committed budget.

2) Staggered prepay tied to performance milestones (hybrid) — what you suggested
  - Example: 30% upfront, 35% at start of Year 2, 35% at start of Year 3
  - Discount: 16–18% effective across term, with standard SLA credits for missed p95/p99 targets
  - Net-90: milestone invoices can carry Net-90 but require finance credit approval and an executed SOW + invoice schedule. We typically require a signed commitment letter and annual reconciliation.

3) Annual prepay ladder (year-by-year prepay with increasing discounts for ramp guarantees)
  - Discount: 12% year 1 (prepay), 14% year 2, 15–16% year 3 with ramped usage guarantees
  - Net-90: each annual invoice can be Net-90 after credit review; less operational risk for us than milestone Net-90 across term.

Notes / constraints:
- Net-90 on milestone invoices: possible but needs credit + legal signoff. For Net-90 we ask for additional protections: parent company guarantee, purchase order, or an initial higher upfront tranche (30–45%).
- SLA credits: we can include service credits that offset future invoices; they do not cancel payment obligations.
- Escrow/third-party guarantees: available as a compromise for larger deals.

I've attached a draft SOW and a pricing model workbook showing how discounts and invoice schedules affect Redwood unit economics. Please review and tell me which structure you prefer — I can get Finance and Legal alignment quickly if you confirm the preferred payment split.
